newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight busier but brings little joy to owners.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight busier but brings little joy to owners.

text.p: Turnover was reasonable on the dry freight market on Wednesday with fair tonnages reported fixed but there was little evidence of a turnaround in shipowners' favour.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) fell by four points to 1,011.
Softening freight rates have yet to stimulate any signifcant improvement in chartering demand for any bulk commodities.

Also bearish was the decline in prices achievable by owners for tonnage sold for scrap in the Far East. Current levels are little more than $165/170 per lightweight tonne compared with close to $200 in July. GRAINS

Brokers said they heard rumours Dreyfus fixed a Caper for wheat from St Lawrence to the Continent for early October at under $5.0. This followed news Cargill fixed four Panamaxes and one Caper Plate and Brazil to the Continent in the last week on private terms. Rates are believed to have fallen from $15.50 basis 2-1 for a Panamax for the first fixture via $14.95 and $14.75 to $14.12 1/2 for the Forum Cape. Pioneer were linked with a Panamax of 61,000 dwt 2.4m cft grain for similar business at $6,000 daily plus $50,000 bonus. Amadeus 66,916 dwt has been covered by grain charterers, possibly Continental, delivery Tubarao early October for two laden legs via Argentina and the Continent. The rate has been estimated at about $7,000 daiuly plus $70,000 bonus.

Dreyfus were also active from this area having covered two September Panamaxes, Kardamyla and Suerte, loading Plate and or Brazil to Philippines and/or China with wide options. Kardamyla wa said fixed 50,000/10 soybean meal basis 2 load/2 discharge at $27.00. Elsewhere UBC were linked with a fixture of 55,000 wheat St Lawrence/Iran at $17.10.

Rates in the mineral trades appeared to ease further in the Atlantic. Cetragpa fixed Esplanade for 100,000 tonnes coal Hampton Roads/Fos for end-Oct at $5.25 and Krupp took Esra 1 for 120,000 tonnes ironore Saldanha Bay/Rotterdam for mid Oct.

Reports of Lowlands Jade 149,000 dwt being fixed by Navix delivery Continent early Oct for a trip via Hampton Roads and Richards Bay to Japan at $14,700 daily were discounted by some brokers who believe the business was covered on voyage basis.
Panamaxes fared little better than Capers in the Atlantic with reports Deiulemar covered Norfolk/Genoa at an economical level and Coe and Clerici fixed Kamsar/Stade bauxite at about $5.50.
Franco British were said to have booked 65,000 tonnes coal Richards Bay/Tarragona for mid Oct at $6.40 and HMM took Halla relet Achilles for Richards Bay/South Korea on private terms.

HANDY SIZES Weak conditions persist in the Western Atlantic. World Achilles Two, 37,000 dwt is believed fixed at a poor rate from U.S. Gulf and Aristotelis 23,286 dwt went to Industrial delivery prompt U.S. Gulf trip China at only $8,600 daily.

Hopes for better rates from the Continent were not justified on the basis of rumoured fixtures. Arete 40,000 dwt to the Far East with unnamed charterers at $10,300 daily, Leo M 29,000 dwt to Von Appen for the same trip at $8,500 daily and a 27,000 dwt vessel in France/North Coast South America at just over $4,000 daily.
In a quiet Far East market NYK agreed a firmer $7,000 daily on subjects for Suitiva 29,000 dwt delivery prompt Singapore for an Australian round.
